prohibited_claims: the public healthcare system is useless or should be avoided entirely
private insurance covers all pre-existing conditions
private hospitals are always clinically better than public hospitals
private insurance guarantees immediate treatment with zero waiting
portability across countries is automatic on every policy
a local plan can never be comprehensive
any fear-based or urgency-manufacturing framing (e.g. implying something bad will happen without this policy)
that international plans generally cover vitamins or supplements without explicit confirmation from the policy wording
required_acknowledgements: the public system plays an essential social-safety-net role, particularly for people who are financially vulnerable, uninsured, or affected by pre-existing-condition underwriting limits elsewhere
some local private plans are genuinely well-designed and may be the more cost-effective, appropriate choice for someone with simple, purely domestic needs
portability, direct billing and other IPMI features must be confirmed against the actual policy wording, not assumed as universal
statistics about unmet needs or out-of-pocket spending describe access barriers and financing patterns — they do not by themselves prove someone was uninsured or that a specific claim was denied

required_distinction.local_private_insurance: can be cost-effective and sufficient for simple, domestic-only needs
required_distinction.ipmi: broader geographic freedom, continuity across relocation, higher limits and international provider choice — valuable when those specific things matter to the applicant
required_distinction.travel_insurance: for temporary trips only, not a substitute for ongoing health cover
